explanation: This slide displays a schematic diagram of a single DNA nucleotide. It labels the three main components: the phosphate group (represented as a circle), the 5-carbon sugar deoxyribose (represented as a pentagon), and a nitrogenous base, which in this diagram is thymine (T) but can also be adenine (A), guanine (G), or cytosine (C).

questions.q: In the diagram of a DNA nucleotide, which component is represented as a pentagon?
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the 5-carbon sugar deoxyribose is represented by the 5-sided pentagon shape in nucleotide diagrams. The phosphate group is represented as a circle (Option A) and the nitrogenous base as a nitrogen-containing ring structure (Option B).
